facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old man
no significant medical history
a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
the lesion had been present since birth and had not changed in size or character
Vital signs were within normal limits
An MRI of the tongue showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue in the midline at the junction of the oral component and base
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal, demonstrated mild contrast enhancement, had intact overlying mucosa, and showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
the sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal

concepts.why: The patient has a midline dorsal tongue lesion that is partly fatty and has mild contrast enhancement, consistent with a lingual thyroid.
The lesion has been present since birth and is a smooth, regular, and soft mass, consistent with a congenital granular cell tumor.
The lesion is partly fatty and likely submucosal, consistent with a lipoma of the tongue.
The lesion is a protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue, consistent with a hamartoma of the tongue.
The lesion has mild contrast enhancement, consistent with a hemangioma of the tongue.
The lesion is a smooth, regular, and soft mass, consistent with a neurofibroma of the tongue.
The lesion is an exophytic mass, consistent with a papilloma of the tongue.
The lesion is a smooth, regular, and soft mass, consistent with a fibroma of the tongue.

rationales.F03: The presence of a smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue is more typical of benign tumors or congenital anomalies.
rationales.F04: The long-standing nature of the lesion since birth suggests a congenital or benign condition.
rationales.F06: The MRI findings of a protuberant mass with intact overlying mucosa are consistent with a benign tumor or congenital anomaly.
rationales.F07: The partly fatty composition and mild contrast enhancement of the lesion are highly suggestive of a lipoma, making it less likely to be other conditions like lingual thyroid or neurofibroma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The lesion's appearance as partly fatty and submucosal with mild contrast enhancement and intact overlying mucosa supports the diagnosis of Lipoma of the Tongue.
